The post 0sec Labs Open-Sources 0, an AI Security Harness With Web UI, CLI and MCP appeared first on MarkTechPost . ]]> Zurich-based 0sec Labs has released 0 , an open-source AI security harness. It runs vulnerability investigations, code review, pentesting, reverse engineering and fix generation. Developers drive it from a local browser console, a headless CLI or an MCP server . The 0sec Labs open-source AI security harness is licensed MIT OR Apache-2.0 and ships as a research preview. TL;DR Wrapper: It is a software harness. Bring your own LLM from 14 listed providers . Runs on: Apple Silicon macOS, x64 or ARM64 Linux, or the ghcr.io/0sec-labs/0 container. No GPU needed. Model inference runs at your provider. Performance: Strong self-reported CTF scores, plus a public record of upstream Linux kernel fixes. Best: 93/95 (97.9%) on XBOW web CTFs, gpt-5.4 cohort, any-success grouping. Worst: Black-box-only XBOW union of 81/104 (77.9%) . A 2026 cold run scored 45/104 (43.3%) . Bottom line: Best: one harness spans web, source, packages, binaries and kernels. Worst: headline scores are self-reported and not pass@1. What is 0 from 0sec Labs? 0 is a control plane around LLMs and security tools. It is not a model. You plug in a provider, and 0 runs scoped workflows against authorized targets. The research team describes it as a self-evolving, multi-model harness . 0sec Labs is backed by Y Combinator . How does the 0 harness work? The architecture docs state one rule: reproduce before trusting. Agentic scans follow a conceptual pipeline: Plan, Discover, Attack: a research agent picks vulnerability classes, maps endpoints and tests hypotheses. Triage: filters remove weak findings and check evidence completeness. Verify: a separate session re-exercises each candidate, with 5 turns per finding. Report: outputs include HTML, PDF, SARIF, Markdown and JSON. Web pentesting is shell-first. The agent uses bash with curl, python3 and sqlmap, not a fixed HTTP tool set. Evidence carries a proof grade from candidate to impact-proven . Compiled targets go through 0verse , a separate in-repo engine. It wraps Ghidra, angr and AFL++. Its local MCP server exposes 9 tools for scanning, triage, PoVs and reports. How do developers use it? Installation is one script. Running 0 opens the local browser console without an account. The console has chat, a findings queue and board, workflow templates, skills and memory. Coding agents connect through 0 mcp-server --workflows . The CLI exposes the same workflow runner with commands like 0 workflow run and 0 runs list . Model access is bring-your-own. The API keys page lists OpenAI, Anthropic, DeepSeek, OpenRouter, Azure, Qwen, Kimi, GLM and Grok. It also supports Claude, Codex and Gemini CLI runtimes. Benchmarks: what do the numbers say? All scores below are self-reported. Benchmark Score Conditions XBOW web CTFs 93/95 (97.9%) gpt-5.4 cohort, any retained success counts XBOW union, white-box 102/104 Retained artifacts, not additive XBOW union, black-box 81/104 Retained artifacts, not additive Cybench 36/40 (90.0%) Azure gpt-5.4, 3 retries npm audit, 81 packages F1 0.973 100% TPR, FPR 0.11, self-built ground truth The recorded cost was about $5.20 per solved XBOW challenge . The research page lists 30+ merged Linux kernel 0-days. Disclosures span Bluetooth, NFC, mac802154, TIPC and mlx5e subsystems. Library CVEs include jsonata, node-forge, protobuf.js and Wireshark. Availability and pricing The open-source harness is free. You pay your model provider. A hosted version, 0cloud , is on a waitlist. The pricing page lists $100 in trial credits and $5 per PR security test. Key Takeaways 0 is an MIT/Apache-2.0 AI security harness from Y Combinator-backed 0sec Labs. It ships a browser console, headless CLI and MCP server for coding agents. Bring your own model: 14 providers plus Claude, Codex and Gemini CLIs. The post Google AI Releases Elephant-Goldfish Model Plugin for Spec-First Coding appeared first on MarkTechPost . ]]> Google has open-sourced the Elephant-Goldfish Model (EGM) plugin , a design-and-review layer for AI coding agents. The Elephant-Goldfish Model plugin makes an agent write a specification before it writes code. Fresh subagents with no conversation history then attack that spec. Google says thousands of its engineers use it . It is quite simple: catch wrong assumptions in a Markdown file, not in a pull request. TL;DR Size: 7 skills, 9 reviewer personas, 6 brainstorm lenses, 5 review stages. No model weights; your agent supplies the LLM. Runs on: any harness that can spawn fresh subagents: Antigravity, Claude Code 2.1.271+, Claude Cowork, Codex, ChatGPT. Uses your existing model quota. Performance: no accuracy benchmark published. Evidence is adoption and end-to-end harness test runs. Best: Codex 0.163.0 completed 15 native fresh-context reviewers in order. 2 live tests passed in 573.13s. Worst: the Claude Cowork run stopped after stages 5 to 7 on a usage limit. Issue #237 reports AGENTS.md leaking into Codex reviewers. Bottom line: best thing, forced independent review before code. Worst thing, heavy token use and unverified isolation on some hosts. What is Google’s Elephant-Goldfish Model plugin? EGM is an Apache 2.0 plugin of skills, reviewer personas and document standards.
